title: Quit Corporate Job to Become Full-Time Indie Game Developer
planText: I am quitting my $130k software engineer job next month to develop a retro pixel-art RPG full-time. I have $25k in savings (about 5 months of living expenses). I have built game prototypes before but never shipped a commercial title. I plan to finish the game in 6 months, launch on Steam, and sustain myself from game sales.

pessimist.headline: Six months is fantasy; you will run out of money at 40% completion.

points.claim: Indie games suffer an average 2-3x timeline overrun due to scope creep.
points.suggestedFix: Cut scope to a vertical slice or 2-hour micro-game first.

points.claim: Five months of savings gives zero buffer for unexpected life emergencies.
points.suggestedFix: Keep at least 12 months of living expenses before resigning.

points.claim: Steam algorithm heavily penalizes unmarketed debuts with no prior wishlist velocity.
points.suggestedFix: Build a Steam page and collect 5,000 wishlists before leaving your job.

pessimist.verdict: High probability of burning out and returning to corporate work in debt.

accountant.headline: Negative expected monetary value without a guaranteed cashflow safety net.

points.claim: $25k savings against $5k/mo burn gives exactly 5 months, but game takes 6 months minimum.
points.suggestedFix: Reduce monthly burn to $2.5k or secure part-time contracting income.

points.claim: Steam takes a 30% cut, plus taxes and asset/tool overhead not budgeted.
points.suggestedFix: Budget $4k for platform fees, localization, and audio licenses.

points.claim: Median Steam game revenue in year 1 is under $1,000.
points.suggestedFix: Model worst-case scenario at $2,000 gross revenue.

accountant.verdict: Financially unviable in its current form without supplemental runway.

skepticalParent.headline: Why throw away a stable, respectable career for uncertain video games?

points.claim: You have health insurance, 401(k) matching, and stability right now.
points.suggestedFix: Work on the game nights and weekends until it proves commercial traction.

points.claim: Explaining an employment gap if the game flops will be difficult.
points.suggestedFix: Frame your indie period as an LLC venture or take an unpaid sabbatical.

skepticalParent.verdict: Irrational risk tolerance when you could easily moon-light the prototype first.

futureYou.headline: You will deeply regret isolating yourself without a launchable milestone.

points.claim: Working solo from home every day leads to severe motivational paralysis by month 3.
points.suggestedFix: Join an indie dev co-working circle or stream development weekly.

points.claim: Shipping nothing after 6 months will crush your creative confidence.
points.suggestedFix: Commit to a public itch.io playtest build within 60 days.

futureYou.verdict: Protect your mental health by establishing rapid external feedback loops.

optimist.headline: Your technical foundation and passion can produce a breakout cult classic.

points.claim: Pixel-art RPGs have dedicated niche communities willing to champion passion projects.
points.suggestedFix: Engage RPG communities on TikTok and Reddit early with devlogs.

points.claim: Software engineering skills give you a massive advantage in clean architecture.
points.suggestedFix: Leverage your engineering speed to polish core gameplay feel.

optimist.verdict: Tremendous upside if you de-risk the financial cliff with phased milestones.

judge.rationale: The original plan faced an immediate liquidity crisis at month 5 with no marketing runway. Hardening the plan around moonlight de-risking and 10-12 months buffer transforms it into a viable venture.
topRisks: Running out of cash before beta release
Steam discovery failure due to zero pre-launch wishlists
Isolation and burnout without intermediate public milestones
judge.hardenedPlan: Phase 1 (Months 1-3 while staying employed): Build a 15-minute vertical slice. Launch Steam page and hit 3,000 wishlists. Save an additional $10k. Phase 2 (Months 4-9): Transition to 20 hr/week consulting ($4k/mo) while spending 30 hr/week finishing the game. Phase 3 (Month 10): Launch during a Steam Next Fest with community backing.

actionItems.task: Create Steam developer account and build capsule art
Build public 15-minute demo and release on itch.io
Secure 1 freelance client for 15 hours/week fallback income

unresolvedQuestions: Can your current living expenses realistically be cut by 30%?
What is your target retail price and estimated unit sales breakeven?
